voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: its questions (מאי, מיבעי ליה, למה לי, אטו, ותו ליכא, מנלן), its unattributed answers and derashot on new lemmas, the narrative of 12b.7-8, 13a.22-23, 16a.4-11, 16a.14, 16a.17, its kashya/teyuvta at 14a.9 and 15a.4
חד אמר (12a.11) -- one of Rav and Shmuel; the text does not say which
וחד אמר (12a.11) -- the other of Rav and Shmuel
במתניתא תנא (12a.11): two doorways
תניא (12a.13): R' Yehuda and R' Nechemya on the couches
R' Yehuda (bar Ilai) as cited in the baraitot of 12a.13, 13a.11, 13a.18, 14b.12, 15b.14
דבי רבי ישמעאל תנא (12a.15)
transmits משום רבי מאיר at 12a.17
R' Elazar (ben Pedat): 12a.18, 13a.20, 13a.24-13b.6, and transmitter of R' Chanina at 15a.16-15b.6
Ahasuerus, whose words the narrators report
Vashti, whose message Rava reports (12b.6)
Haman, whose words Rava (13b.16-19) and the stam's narrative (16a.4-10) report
the guests at the feast (12b.3), as Rava reports them
the Rabbis whom Ahasuerus asked to judge Vashti (12b.7-8), as the stam narrates
במתניתא תנא (12b.5): Gabriel made her a tail
the ministering angels whose pleas R' Levi reports (12b.10)
תנא (12b.11): Memuchan is Haman
אמרי (12b.13): the recipients of the first letters, in Rava's account
Rebbi (12b.14-15), and 'רבינו' of the tanna at 14a.12
King David, speaker in the Avigail narrative (14a.22-14b.2)

props.gloss_en: one of Rav and Shmuel: 'in the court of the garden of the king's palace' (Esth 1:5) -- each guest was placed in court, garden or palace as befitted him
the other: he seated them in the court and it did not hold them, in the garden and it did not hold them, until he brought them into the palace and it held them
a baraita: he seated them in the court and opened two doorways for them, one to the garden and one to the palace
what is 'chur' (Esth 1:6)? Rav: [a fabric of] holes upon holes
Shmuel: he spread white wool for them
'karpas': R' Yosei bar Chanina -- cushions of strips
R' Yehuda: 'couches of gold and silver' (Esth 1:6) -- one fit for silver [sat on] silver, one fit for gold on gold
R' Nechemya: rather, they were of silver and their legs of gold
R' Nechemya to R' Yehuda: if so, you cast jealousy into the feast
'bahat and marble': R' Asi -- stones that vie for their owners
and so it says: 'crown stones glittering upon his land' (Zech 9:16)
'dar vesocharet': Rav -- rows upon rows
Shmuel: there is a gem in the coastal cities called 'dara'; he set it in the middle of the feast and it lit for them like noon
the school of R' Yishmael taught: he proclaimed release for all merchants
the verse: 'and vessels differing from vessels' (Esth 1:7) -- quoted as the object of the stam's difficulty
Rava: a heavenly voice went forth and said to them: the first ones perished on account of My vessels, and you repeat [use] them!
'and royal wine in abundance': Rav -- this teaches that he gave each one to drink wine older than himself
'according to the law' (Esth 1:8) -- as the law of the Torah: as in the Torah's law eating exceeds drinking, so at that wicked one's feast eating exceeded drinking
'none compelled': R' Elazar -- this teaches that he gave each one wine of his own country
'to do according to the will of each man': Rava -- the will of Mordechai and Haman
Mordechai, for it is written 'a Jewish man' (Esth 2:5); Haman -- 'a man, adversary and enemy' (Esth 7:6)
the verse: 'also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house' (Esth 1:9) -- object of the stam's difficulty
Rava: both of them intended a matter of sin
Rava: this is the folk saying: he with gourds, and his wife with squash
the verse: 'on the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine' (Esth 1:10) -- object of the stam's אטו
Rava: the seventh day was Shabbat
when Israel eat and drink they begin with words of Torah and praise; when the nations eat and drink they begin only with words of frivolity
the guests: these said Median women are beautiful, those said Persian women are beautiful
Ahasuerus: the vessel I use is neither Median nor Persian but Chaldean -- do you wish to see her?
they said to him: yes, provided she is naked
for with the measure a person measures he is measured: this teaches that the wicked Vashti would bring Jewish girls, strip them naked and make them work on Shabbat
this is what is written: 'he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what was decreed upon her' (Esth 2:1) -- as she did, so was decreed upon her
the verse: 'and Queen Vashti refused' (Esth 1:12) -- object of the stam's difficulty
R' Yosei bar Chanina: this teaches that leprosy broke out on her
a baraita: Gabriel came and made her a tail
Vashti sent to him: son of my father's stableman! my father drank against a thousand and did not get drunk, and that man is made a fool by his wine
Rava: [he burned so] because of what she sent him; at once 'his anger burned in him'
who are 'the wise men' (Esth 1:13)? the Rabbis
'who knew the times' -- who know to intercalate years and fix months
Ahasuerus to them: judge her for me
the Rabbis deliberated: if we say kill her, tomorrow his wine wears off and he will demand her of us; if we say let her be, she slights the kingship
the Rabbis to him: since the Temple was destroyed and we were exiled from our land, counsel was taken from us and we cannot judge capital cases; go to Ammon and Moab
and they gave him the reason, as written: 'Moab has been at ease from his youth... therefore his taste remains in him' (Jer 48:11)
R' Levi: this entire verse (Esth 1:14, the seven ministers' names) was said on account of the offerings

the ministering angels said before the Holy One: did they [the gentiles] offer You yearling rams (karshena), two turtledoves (shetar), build an altar of earth (admata), serve in priestly garments with tarshish, stir blood (meres), stir meal-offerings (marsena), prepare a table (memuchan)?
a tanna: Memuchan is Haman; why is he called Memuchan? for he is prepared (muchan) for calamity
Rav Kahana: hence the commoner leaps to the head [speaks first]
Rava: were it not for the first letters ('every man should rule in his house', Esth 1:22), no remnant of Israel's 'enemies' would have survived
they said: what is this he sent us, 'every man should rule in his house'? obviously -- even a weaver is commander in his own house!
Rebbi: 'every prudent man acts with knowledge' (Prov 13:16) is David ('let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin', 1 Kgs 1:2) -- whoever had a daughter brought her to him
'and a fool spreads folly' is Ahasuerus, as written 'let the king appoint officers' (Esth 2:3) -- whoever had a daughter hid her from him
